summary: Jefferson County summit lookout in use from the 1910s to 1967; cupola collapsed in 1982 and remains are on the summit within the Warm Springs Reservation.

facts.status_note: Cupola collapsed in 1982; the rocky base and a few weathered timbers remain on the summit

access.note: The summit lies within the Warm Springs Reservation. A hiking guide lists no fees or permits. The former National Forest trail is no longer officially maintained.

visit.trail_note: Reached by a former National Forest trail that is no longer officially maintained

events.note: A lookout point was set up, with an Osborne fire-finder installed on a post
Lumber lookout structure, 7 by 10 feet, completed July 30, 1913 per a 1958 historical file; built by Bush Osborne
30-foot steel windmill tower with 6x6 cab and tent cabin (register and firelookout.com)
John Lewis went up as lookout for the summer (Maupin Times item)
W.E. Curran resumed his duties as lookout
Fire on Woodside Point reported July 5 by Lookout Curran; started from blasting on the Clackamas River trail; put out by midnight
Calvin Burnside announced as summer lookout, a job he had held the season before
Forest Service stopped using the lookout; cabin abandoned
About 61,360 acres of Mount Hood and Willamette forest land placed in the Warm Springs Reservation, lookout included
Cupola fell through the roof; remains left on the summit

corrections.why: The register and firelookout.com describe a 30-foot steel windmill tower, and a 1929 item calls the structure a new tower. Outdoorpilgrim describes a 7-by-10 structure on a rock base, so the structure type is disputed; medium confidence.
No source found says a permit is required. Outdoorpilgrim lists no fees or permits, and the summit lies within the reservation, so restricted is the closest supported level.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1958 historical file (quoted on Rex's page) and outdoorpilgrim put a 7-by-10-foot lumber structure on the summit in 1913. The register and firelookout.com put a 30-foot steel windmill tower there in 1915. Both are recorded as events.
The register and outdoorpilgrim say the cupola collapsed through the roof in 1982. Oregon Hikers says the wooden lookout was later blown off its foundation in a windstorm. Both accounts are recorded.

notes_for_editor: Two accounts of the first structure conflict (1913 lumber cabin vs 1915 steel windmill tower) and both are kept. Access corrected from permission to restricted because no source found requires a permit. The brief's kind 'ground' is disputed; height_m 9.1 comes from the register's 30-foot tower figure only. The story is about 320 words. Oregon Hikers and Outdoor Pilgrim are trip guides, not records, so their statements about access and remains are attributed to them.
